name: Bernard Thévenet
milestone_by_age_26: Won a stage at the 1970 Tour de France as a neo-professional and followed with multiple Tour stages, Tour de Romandie (1972), and the French national road race championship (1973) by age 25.
early_history_summary: Born to a farming family in rural Burgundy, Thévenet was inspired watching the Tour de France pass through his village at age 13. He became Burgundy champion at 17 and French junior champion at 20, then joined the ACBB development club which fed into the Peugeot professional team. He turned professional with Peugeot in 1970 and won a Tour de France mountain stage in his very first Tour as a last-minute stand-in.
family_context_summary: Born to a farming family in Saint-Julien-de-Civry, Burgundy; his parents needed him on the farm and were initially unsupportive of his racing ambitions.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no evidence of family cycling background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: ACBB development pipeline,Peugeot team,rural farming background,climbing talent
evidence_summary: Thévenet grew up on a farm in Burgundy with no family cycling background, but the ACBB club in Paris served as a recognized development pipeline into the Peugeot professional team. He was champion of Burgundy at 17 and French junior champion at 20, showing strong early physical talent as a climber. His parents were initially resistant to his racing but relented after he won races. By 25 he had won multiple Tour de France stages, Tour de Romandie, and the French national championship.
starting_point: Born to a farming family in Saint-Julien-de-Civry, Burgundy, France; parents were farmers with no cycling background.
current_position: Retired former professional cyclist; two-time Tour de France winner (1975, 1977); now age 78 and living in France.

trajectory.event: Won French junior national cycling championship and joined the ACBB development team.
Won the Tour de l'Avenir, a major amateur stage race.

Won Tour de Romandie and two stages of the Tour de France.
Won the French national road race championship and finished second overall at the Tour de France.
Won his first Tour de France, ending Eddy Merckx's five-year reign.
Won his second Tour de France title.
Retired from professional cycling after a final season.

name: Bojana Popović
milestone_by_age_26: Won the EHF Women's Champions League with Slagelse DT in 2004 (age 25) and was the tournament's top scorer with 98 goals, repeating both feats in 2005.
early_history_summary: Born in Niš, Yugoslavia, Popović started playing handball at age 11 following her older sister. Her coach Miško Djordjević at DIN Niš focused on player development over results. She moved to Budućnost Podgorica at 18 and won four consecutive Yugoslav League titles before signing with Danish powerhouse Slagelse DT in 2002, where she became a Champions League winner and top scorer.
family_context_summary: Born in Niš, Serbia (then Yugoslavia); her older sister Marija started handball first and Bojana followed at age 11. No information on parental occupation or financial status found.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no evidence of family handball background beyond sister's involvement.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early start at 11,developmental coach,sister handball,Slagelse DT pipeline
evidence_summary: Popović started handball at 11 in Niš, guided by a development-focused coach and inspired by her older sister. She was a key player at DIN Niš as a teenager before moving to Budućnost at 18, where she won four consecutive league titles. Her move to Slagelse DT in Denmark gave her access to the strongest women's handball league and coach Anja Andersen, leading to Champions League titles and top-scorer honors by 25. Family financial background is not documented.
starting_point: Born in Niš, Yugoslavia (now Serbia) in 1979; followed her older sister into handball at age 11; family financial background not documented.
current_position: Retired handball player; head coach of Montenegrin women's national team and assistant coach of Danish national team; considered one of the best female handball players of the 2000s.

trajectory.event: Began senior handball career at DIN Niš in the Yugoslav league.

Led Montenegro women's national team to historic bronze at EHF EURO 2022 as head coach.

name: Milena Canonero
milestone_by_age_26: Designed the iconic costumes for Stanley Kubrick's landmark film A Clockwork Orange (1971), her first major screen credit, at approximately age 25.
early_history_summary: Born in Turin, Italy, Canonero studied fashion, period design, and art history at university in Genoa before moving to England in the late 1960s. She designed for friends' London boutiques and assisted on commercials, meeting filmmakers along the way. By chance she was invited to watch Kubrick shoot 2001: A Space Odyssey, and the director asked her to collaborate on his next feature, A Clockwork Orange.
family_context_summary: Born in Turin, Italy; attended university in Genoa studying fashion, period design, and art history. No information on parental occupation or financial status found in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Kubrick mentorship,London film scene,art history education,boutique design experience
evidence_summary: Canonero studied fashion and art history in Genoa before moving to London in the late 1960s, where she worked in boutiques and commercials. Her chance encounter with Stanley Kubrick on the set of 2001 led to her first film credit on A Clockwork Orange (1971), a landmark collaboration that launched her career. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources. Note: birth year is disputed between 1946 (IMDb, LOC) and 1949 (Wikipedia).
starting_point: Born in Turin, Italy; studied fashion, period design, and art history at university in Genoa before moving to England in the late 1960s; family financial background not documented.
current_position: Retired Italian costume designer with four Academy Awards; received Honorary Golden Bear at Berlinale 2017; married to actor Marshall Bell.

trajectory.event: Designed costumes for Stanley Kubrick's A Clockwork Orange, her first major film credit.

Won second Academy Award for Chariots of Fire, whose 1920s designs inspired a fashion trend.
Won third Academy Award for Marie Antoinette, directed by Sofia Coppola.
Won fourth Academy Award for The Grand Budapest Hotel, directed by Wes Anderson.

name: Manuel Blum
milestone_by_age_26: Completed his Ph.D. in mathematics at MIT under Marvin Minsky in 1964, having already worked in Warren McCulloch's neurophysiology lab on computational models of the brain.
early_history_summary: Born in Caracas, Venezuela to parents who had fled Europe in the 1930s, Blum came to the US in the mid-1950s to study electrical engineering at MIT. As a junior he joined Warren McCulloch's neurophysiology lab, then pursued mathematical logic and recursion theory for insights into computation and brains. He completed his doctorate under AI pioneer Marvin Minsky in 1964.
family_context_summary: Born in Caracas, Venezuela in 1938; parents settled there after fleeing Europe in the 1930s. He describes himself as 'the opposite of a prodigy.' No information on parental occupation found.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; parents were European refugees who settled in Venezuela.
evidence_summary: Blum was born in Venezuela to European refugee parents and came to MIT in the mid-1950s to study electrical engineering. At MIT he gained access to McCulloch's neurophysiology lab and then Minsky as his doctoral advisor, placing him at the epicenter of early AI and computational complexity research. He completed his PhD at 26, launching a career that would earn the Turing Award in 1995. Family financial details are not documented, but the MIT ecosystem provided exceptional mentorship and intellectual infrastructure.
starting_point: Born in Caracas, Venezuela in 1938 to European refugee parents who fled in the 1930s; came to the US in the mid-1950s to attend MIT.
current_position: Bruce Nelson Professor of Computer Science at Carnegie Mellon University; Turing Award winner (1995); retired from UC Berkeley in 2001.

trajectory.event: Completed Ph.D. in mathematics at MIT under Marvin Minsky, having worked in McCulloch's neurophysiology lab.
Joined the faculty at UC Berkeley as assistant professor, later becoming a leading figure in computational complexity theory.
Received the ACM A.M. Turing Award for contributions to computational complexity theory and cryptography.
Joined Carnegie Mellon University as Bruce Nelson Professor of Computer Science.

name: Gun Röring
milestone_by_age_26: Won an Olympic gold medal in the team portable apparatus event at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics at age 22.
early_history_summary: Born in Umeå, Sweden, Röring was a member of the Swedish women's gymnastics team that competed at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics. She placed 23rd in the individual all-around but was part of the Swedish octet that won gold in the team portable apparatus event, a now-defunct discipline similar to modern rhythmic gymnastics. She competed for club GF Ryck In in Umeå.
family_context_summary: Born in Umeå, Västerbotten, Sweden; no information on parental occupation or financial status found in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Swedish national gymnastics team,GF Ryck In club,team event
evidence_summary: Röring was a gymnast from Umeå, Sweden, competing for club GF Ryck In. She was selected for the Swedish women's gymnastics team at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics, where the team won gold in the portable apparatus event. Little is documented about her early training, family background, or coaching. The Swedish team entered the Olympics as reigning World Champions, indicating a strong national gymnastics program.
starting_point: Born in Umeå, Västerbotten, Sweden in 1930; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Died on March 17, 2006 in Umeå, Sweden at age 75; final known role was as a retired gymnast and Olympic gold medalist.

trajectory.event: Won Olympic gold medal in team portable apparatus at the Helsinki Olympics with the Swedish women's gymnastics team.
Died on March 17, 2006 in Umeå, Sweden.

name: Rinat Akhmetov
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: By age 26 (1992), Akhmetov had just co-founded ARS, a small coal-to-coke trading company; his major wealth came from large-scale privatization acquisitions in 1998-99 and the founding of SCM in 2000.
early_history_summary: Born in Donetsk to a working-class family (father a coal miner, mother a shop assistant), Akhmetov entered business in the early 1990s after the collapse of the Soviet Union, trading industrial raw materials. He co-founded ARS in 1992 to process coal into coke, but his empire was built through acquiring state assets during Ukraine's privatization era in the late 1990s.
family_context_summary: Born in Donetsk, Ukrainian SSR to a working-class family; father was a coal miner and mother a shop assistant; ethnic Volga Tatar and practicing Sunni Muslim.

His wealth was built through acquiring privatized state assets in the late 1990s, founding SCM in 2000. No material milestone by age 26 is documented; his rise to wealth came after 26.

name: Monica Bellucci
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: By age 26 (1990), Bellucci had made her acting debut in minor TV and film roles; her breakthrough came at age 32 with The Apartment (1996), which earned a César nomination. International fame arrived with Malèna (2000) at age 36.

She made her acting debut in 1990 in Italian TV and film, but her breakthrough role came in The Apartment (1996).
family_context_summary: Born in Città di Castello, Umbria, Italy; father owned a trucking company and mother was a painter. She was an only child raised in a Catholic household.

name: Mihaela Peneș
milestone_by_age_26: Won a surprise Olympic gold medal in the javelin throw at the 1964 Tokyo Olympics at age 17, becoming the third woman to throw over 60 meters.
early_history_summary: Born in Bucharest, Romania, Peneș trained in swimming, handball, and basketball before switching to athletics influenced by her mother, a former athlete. She won the national junior championships in 1963 setting a national record, then debuted internationally at the 1964 Olympics where she won gold at just 17 years old. She was coached by Ioan Benga at CS Dinamo București.
family_context_summary: Born in Bucharest, Romania; her mother was a former athlete who influenced her to take up athletics. No information on father's occupation or financial status found.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was a former athlete who influenced Mihaela's switch to athletics; no further details on family athletic background documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: CS Dinamo București,mother athlete influence,coach Ioan Benga,national junior record
evidence_summary: Peneș grew up in Bucharest with a mother who was a former athlete, providing early domain exposure. She trained in multiple sports before specializing in javelin, winning the national junior championship at 16 with a national record. The Romanian sports system placed her at CS Dinamo București under coach Ioan Benga, and she won Olympic gold at 17 in 1964. Her mother's athletic background and the Romanian state sports pipeline were the key early advantages.
starting_point: Born in Bucharest, Romania in 1947; mother was a former athlete who influenced her career; family financial background not documented.
current_position: Died on August 29, 2024 at age 77; former Romanian Olympic Committee Secretary General (1999) and javelin thrower.

name: Mohammed Gammoudi
milestone_by_age_26: Won double gold in the 5,000m and 10,000m at the 1963 Mediterranean Games (age 25) and Olympic silver in the 10,000m at the 1964 Tokyo Olympics (age 26).
early_history_summary: Born in Sidi Aïch, Tunisia to a modest farming family, Gammoudi discovered running after volunteering for the Tunisian Army in his late teens. An officer, Hassine Hammouda, took him under his wing and guided his early development. He won his first military cross-country race in 1961 and rapidly progressed to international competition, winning double gold at the 1963 Mediterranean Games and Olympic silver in 1964.
family_context_summary: Born in Sidi Aïch, Tunisia to a modest farming family of eight brothers; two younger brothers were also cross-country runners. No information on parental occupation beyond farming found.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no evidence of family athletic background beyond brothers' running.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Tunisian Army pipeline,modest farming family,officer mentor Hassine Hammouda,post-independence Tunisia
evidence_summary: Gammoudi came from a modest farming family in rural Tunisia and discovered his talent through the army, where officer Hassine Hammouda became his mentor. Tunisia's independence in 1956 created a hunger for national heroes, providing context for his rise. He won double gold at the 1963 Mediterranean Games and Olympic silver at 26 in 1964. His background offered little financial advantage but the military sports pipeline and his own physical talent drove his early success.
starting_point: Born in Sidi Aïch, Tunisia in 1938 to a modest farming family of eight brothers; discovered running through the Tunisian Army in his late teens.
current_position: Retired Tunisian long-distance runner; Tunisia's first Olympic champion; now age 88 and living in Tunisia.

trajectory.event: Won his first military cross-country race in the Tunisian Army, launching his running career.

Won Olympic silver in the 5,000m at the Munich Olympics, his fourth Olympic medal.

name: Judea Pearl
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: By age 26 (1962), Pearl had completed a BS in Electrical Engineering from the Technion (1960) and an MS from Newark College of Engineering (1961), and was working as a Member of Technical Staff at RCA Research Laboratories. His PhD came in 1965 at age 29, and his foundational work on Bayesian networks and causal reasoning came decades later.
early_history_summary: Born in Bnei Brak, Israel in 1936, Pearl was educated by German refugee scientists who taught in Israeli high schools. He served in the Israeli army, joined a kibbutz, then studied electrical engineering at the Technion, graduating in 1960. He moved to the US for graduate study, earning an MS in 1961 and working at RCA Research Labs before completing his PhD at the Polytechnic Institute of Brooklyn in 1965.
family_context_summary: Born in Bnei Brak, Israel in 1936; his high school and college teachers were top-notch scientists who had emigrated from Germany in the 1930s and taught in high schools because they could not find academic positions.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no evidence of family academic or scientific background.
evidence_summary: Pearl grew up in Israel, benefiting from an exceptional education provided by German refugee scientists teaching in high schools. He completed his BS at the Technion by 24 and MS by 25, then worked at RCA Research Labs. However, his PhD (1965) and the foundational work on Bayesian networks and causal reasoning that earned him the Turing Award came well after age 26. No material milestone by 26 is documented.

name: Liviu Librescu
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: By age 26 (1956), Librescu had graduated from Politehnica University of Bucharest (1952) and was working as a researcher at the Bucharest Institute of Applied Mechanics. His PhD came in 1969 at age 39, and his international academic prominence came after emigrating to Israel in 1978.
early_history_summary: Born in Ploiești, Romania to a Jewish family, Librescu survived the Holocaust as a child, interned in a labor camp in Transnistria and later a ghetto in Focșani. After the war, he studied aerospace engineering at Politehnica University of Bucharest, graduating in 1952, and worked as a researcher at the Institute of Applied Mechanics from 1953. His career was stalled under communist rule because he refused to join the Communist Party.
family_context_summary: Born in 1930 to a Jewish family in Ploiești, Romania; father Isidore Librescu was deported to a labor camp in Transnistria during WWII. The family was interned in a ghetto in Focșani.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no evidence of family engineering or academic background.
evidence_summary: Librescu survived the Holocaust as a child in Romania, then studied aerospace engineering at Politehnica University of Bucharest, graduating at 22. By 26 he was a researcher at the Institute of Applied Mechanics, but his PhD came at 39 and his prominent international career began only after emigrating to Israel in 1978. No material milestone by age 26 is documented; his early career was constrained by communist-era restrictions.

name: Caitlyn Jenner
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1974 AAU decathlon title (age 25) and the 1975 Pan American Games decathlon gold medal while setting a world record of 8,524 points (age 25-26), establishing herself as the world's top decathlete before the 1976 Olympics.
early_history_summary: Born in Mount Kisco, New York, Jenner excelled at multiple sports in high school including pole vault, winning state titles. A football scholarship to Graceland College in Iowa led to a knee injury, after which track coach L.D. Weldon convinced Jenner to try the decathlon. Jenner debuted at the 1970 Drake Relays, made the 1972 Olympic team, then moved to San Jose to train intensively 6-8 hours daily while selling insurance at night, with wife Chrystie supporting the family as a flight attendant.
family_context_summary: Born in Mount Kisco, New York; father William Hugh Jenner was an arborist originally from New Brunswick, Canada; mother Esther Ruth (née McGuire). Jenner was diagnosed with dyslexia as a child. Younger brother Burt was killed in a car accident in 1976.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no evidence of family athletic background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: coach L.D. Weldon,San Jose training hub,intense 6-8hr daily training,multi-sport high school background
evidence_summary: Jenner grew up in a middle-class family in New York and Connecticut, excelling at multiple sports in high school. The pivotal moment was Graceland College coach L.D. Weldon's encouragement to switch from football to decathlon after a knee injury. After the 1972 Olympics, Jenner moved to San Jose to train with individual-event stars under coach Bert Bonanno, training 6-8 hours daily while supported by wife Chrystie's income. This intense concentration and access to the San Jose athletics hub drove rapid improvement to world-record level by 25.
starting_point: Born in Mount Kisco, New York in 1949; father was an arborist from New Brunswick, Canada; mother was Esther Ruth (née McGuire); middle-class family.
current_position: Retired Olympic decathlete and media personality; publicly came out as transgender in 2015; estimated net worth ~$100M; ran for California governor in 2021 recall election.

trajectory.event: Debuted in decathlon at the Drake Relays, finishing fifth with a school-record 6,991 points.

Publicly came out as a transgender woman, announcing the name Caitlyn Marie Jenner.
Ran as a Republican candidate in the California gubernatorial recall election, finishing 13th with 1% of the vote.
